__comment__: EconomyX — phone hold poses. ONE file drives all 26 phones, because every
phone geometry uses a single bone named 'phone'.
THE MODEL IS ANCHORED BY THE GEOMETRY, NOT BY THIS FILE
Each phone geometry's root bone carries
"binding": "q.item_slot_to_bone_name(context.item_slot)"
which is what actually pins the model into the hand — main_hand resolves to
the player's rightItem bone, off_hand to leftItem. Before that binding
existed the model was not attached to the hand at all: Bedrock drew it in the
player's own model space, which is why the handset floated near the feet and
the playing cards sat between the legs.
Because the bone pivot is [0,0,0] and it now lands ON the hand, this file
needs NO position offset. The old values here were compensating for the
broken placement and are gone. Keep position at [0,0,0] unless you are
deliberately nudging the grip.
WHICH WAY DOES THE PHONE FACE (confirmed correct in testing — do not change)
In all 9 models the camera-bump cubes sit at negative Z, so -Z is the BACK
and +Z is the SCREEN. In item-bone space -Z points the way the holder faces,
so at yaw 0 the cameras point out at everyone else and the screen points back
at the holder. That is why both poses below use a Y rotation of 0.
The geometry runs from y=-5.28 to y=+11.22 with the origin at the lower
third, where a hand actually grips, so roughly a third of the body sits below
the hand and two thirds above it. At scale 0.5 that is about 2.6 units below
and 5.6 above.
